nodes.label: C4 — proxy signOut() cookie/response-object mismatch
nodes.rationale: signOut() wrote clear-cookies to res, but the function returned a different NextResponse.redirect() object, so the browser stayed signed in and the next visit triggered an infinite redirect loop. Fixed via a redirectWithCookies() helper that copies res.cookies onto the redirect — same bug class as the /auth/callback fix.

nodes.label: Audit-insert-last, same-transaction rule
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md pivot-era hard rule: any transaction writing audit_events emits the audit event as the LAST statement before commit, since the chain trigger holds pg_advisory_xact_lock until commit — guarantees lock order == chain_seq order == chain order.

nodes.label: BASELINE-DELTAS §3.2 — chain_seq drawn inside advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Identity defaults evaluate at tuple formation before BEFORE triggers fire, so a pre-assigned chain_seq's order need not match lock-acquisition order; overwriting chain_seq inside the advisory lock guarantees correct ordering.
nodes.norm_label: baseline-deltas §3.2 — chain_seq drawn inside advisory lock

nodes.label: CPD Sprint 2 — Design: Security wrapper + audit path + attendee identity
nodes.norm_label: cpd sprint 2 — design: security wrapper + audit path + attendee identity

nodes.label: D1 — Restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated EXECUTE)
nodes.rationale: Closes the audit-authenticity gap from Sprint 1: a malicious authenticated user could forge a legitimately-chained row with false actor claims by calling write_audit_event directly via PostgREST. Every audited mutation instead becomes a SECURITY DEFINER fn ending in the audit write; the postgres-owned definer inherits audit_writer's EXECUTE, so legitimate paths are unaffected.
nodes.norm_label: d1 — restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated execute)

nodes.label: ADR Finding 1 — PostgREST RPCs run as separate transactions
nodes.rationale: An app-level wrapper calling write_audit_event after a mutation runs the audit write in a separate transaction, violating audit-insert-last-same-transaction; forces the SECURITY DEFINER gate→mutation→audit-write-LAST shape.
nodes.norm_label: adr finding 1 — postgrest rpcs run as separate transactions

nodes.label: P2 — Global audit-chain lock discipline
nodes.rationale: The audit chain serializes all writes through one global advisory lock held for transaction duration; audited definer functions must complete slow work before the audit-write and have no side effects between audit-write and commit.

nodes.label: P3 — Behaviour-preserving TDD on rewritten surfaces
nodes.rationale: Check-in and event-publish are shipped surfaces converted to definer functions; capture current behaviour before rewrite, rewrite, re-run same tests, name any intentional delta (per-IP to per-event rate-limit change).

nodes.rationale: Q25 already locked recognition at the ledger level via event dual-accreditation; default is practitioner-declared only, no automation, which is the system's state without any 3b work.

nodes.label: Event Lifecycle decision-state machine
nodes.rationale: Five stored states (draft, pending_body_review, published, credited, cancelled) locked in Q23 item 4; attestation_status is a field on published events, not a separate state.

nodes.label: CPD Sprint 3b Engine Outline
nodes.rationale: Covers the engine that turns attendance into compliant credits, the MVP critical path, double-gated on Q26 plus the external body review; exists so the engine is designable fast once gates lift.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Open-Framework Line
nodes.rationale: Config/data layer fully open now; governance layer open interfaces with defaults; evaluator layer a bounded-grammar interpreter, NOT a general rules engine, extended on documented demand only.

nodes.label: body_rules versioned config DDL (E1)
nodes.rationale: Append-only effective-dated rule versions (effective_from + version_seq, active derived by query); rule content ungated (verified vs 8 bodies), versioning mechanism Q26-shaped.

nodes.label: Deterministic Evaluator evaluate_compliance() (E2)
nodes.rationale: Pure deterministic function projecting a licence's ledger against the body_rules version in force at each entry's valid_domain_time; no AI, no mutation; the single largest unbuilt engine unknown.

nodes.label: Bounded-Grammar Interpreter discipline
nodes.rationale: Evaluator interprets a fixed grammar (floors/caps/cores/units/cycle windows), not arbitrary logic; a body needing logic outside the grammar gets the grammar extended to their documented rule, not a configurable engine.

nodes.label: HKCR 16-subtype passive/active cap stress test
nodes.rationale: Storing 16 activity types is trivial; the evaluator must compute a passive/active cap aggregated across them under the rule version in force at each date; if it handles HKCR it handles the eight verified bodies.

nodes.label: Q26 Config-Hash Fork
nodes.rationale: Pinned-in-hash vs chained-version-table; decided from one behavioural fact (how a body handles mid-cycle rule changes); the single gate that unblocks E1-versioning, E5 and E2 in sequence.

nodes.label: Q27 Evaluator-Versioning
nodes.rationale: For a reproducible historical verdict the evaluator's own version (release tag/code hash) must be pinnable alongside the config version; decide when the first verdict is exported.

nodes.label: RFC 8785 canonical serialization
nodes.rationale: Applied before any config hash regardless of which Q26 arm wins; both arms hash canonicalized config, only where differs.

nodes.label: Bitemporal rule-version evaluation (valid_domain_time)
nodes.rationale: A December activity is judged under December's rules even if evaluated in March.

nodes.label: Issuance: attendance x rules to ledger entries (E3)
nodes.rationale: On published-to-credited transition a deterministic job reads attendance x the body_rules version in force and writes credit_earned via record_credit_entry; store all credits incl. unmatched-body cases, filter in a view, never drop silently.

nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: A checklist validates the requirements text, not the implementation. If the spec is code written in English, the checklist is its unit-test suite; items starting with Verify/Test/Confirm about system behaviour are explicitly prohibited because they silently convert a requirements-quality gate into a QA plan.

nodes.label: Requirement Quality Dimensions
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage — the five axes every checklist item must evaluate, used as the category scaffolding for generated checklists.

nodes.label: 80% Traceability Rule
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: At least 80% of checklist items must carry a spec-section reference or a [Gap]/[Ambiguity]/[Conflict]/[Assumption] marker, so findings can be traced back to the artifact they indict.

nodes.label: Dynamic Clarifying Question Generation
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Up to three signal-derived questions (max five with escalation), never from a pre-baked catalog, and only where the answer materially changes checklist content.

nodes.label: Ambiguity & Coverage Taxonomy
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Ten categories (functional scope, domain/data model, interaction/UX, non-functional quality, integrations, edge cases, constraints/tradeoffs, terminology, completion signals, placeholders) each scored Clear/Partial/Missing to build a prioritization map.

nodes.label: Five-Question Clarification Quota
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Hard cap of five questions asked strictly one at a time, ranked by Impact x Uncertainty, with a recommended answer surfaced first so the user can accept with 'yes'. Unasked high-impact categories must be flagged as Deferred rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Clarifications Session Log
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Each accepted answer is appended as a Q/A bullet under '### Session YYYY-MM-DD' AND immediately applied to the owning spec section; the spec is saved after every integration to minimise context-loss risk, and invalidated earlier statements are replaced rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: Spec Quality Checklist Re-validation
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Only the [ ]/[x] marker of checkbox lines whose state actually changed may be rewritten, preserving case and ordering to avoid noisy diffs; before/after counts plus newly-passing and regressed items are reported.

nodes.label: Constitution Semantic Versioning Policy
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: MAJOR for backward-incompatible principle removals/redefinitions, MINOR for added or materially expanded guidance, PATCH for clarifications. Ambiguous bumps must have their reasoning proposed before finalising.

nodes.label: Sync Impact Report
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Prepended as an HTML comment inside the constitution itself so the amendment trail (version delta, renamed principles, templates updated vs pending, deferred TODOs) travels with the governing document rather than in a side file.

nodes.label: Consistency Propagation Checklist
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: A constitution amendment is not done until plan-template, spec-template, tasks-template, every installed speckit command file, and runtime guidance docs have been re-read and realigned — converting a passive checklist into active validations.

nodes.label: Append-Only Never-Rewrite Contract
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: The only permitted write is appending a new '## Phase N: Convergence' section to tasks.md. Existing tasks are never renumbered, reordered or deleted, spec.md/plan.md are never touched, and when nothing remains tasks.md must stay byte-for-byte unchanged (no empty header) so a clean run leaves zero diff.

nodes.label: Gap Type Classification (missing/partial/contradicts/unrequested)
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: 'unrequested' code is surfaced for awareness only — converge appends a task to review/justify it and never deletes code itself.

nodes.label: Intent Inventory & Code-Scope Map
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Assessment scope is bounded to files named in plan.md/tasks.md plus keyword search for the described concepts; converge deliberately assesses present state and uses no git history or branch comparison.

nodes.label: Phase N: Convergence Task Append Contract
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: New IDs continue from the maximum existing ID (zero-padded T###), each task carries a <source-ref> back to FR/SC/US-AC/plan decision/Constitution principle plus its gap-type, and constitution violations are emitted first as CRITICAL.
nodes.norm_label: phase n: convergence task append contract

nodes.label: Checklist Completion Gate
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Every file under checklists/ is counted into a PASS/FAIL table; any incomplete item halts execution and requires an explicit yes/no from the user before implementation continues — an advisory stop, not a hard block.

nodes.label: Ignore File Detection and Provisioning
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Detects git/Docker/ESLint/Prettier/Terraform/Helm/npm setups and creates or tops-up the matching ignore file from a per-language pattern catalogue; existing files are only appended to, never replaced.

nodes.label: Phase-by-Phase Execution Rules
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Complete each phase before the next, run [P] tasks together but serialize same-file tasks, tests before their implementation, halt on any non-parallel failure while continuing surviving parallel tasks, and mark each finished task [X] in tasks.md.

nodes.label: Phase 0: Outline & Research
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Every NEEDS CLARIFICATION becomes a dispatched research task; findings consolidate into research.md as Decision / Rationale / Alternatives considered, so the reason a choice was made survives into planning.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Design & Contracts
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Produces data-model.md, contracts/ and quickstart.md. Contracts are skipped for purely internal projects; quickstart stays a runnable validation guide and must not carry implementation bodies, migrations or full test suites.

nodes.label: SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY Resolution
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Spec directory name and git branch name are deliberately independent. Prefix comes from init-options.json feature_numbering (sequential NNN or timestamp); branch_numbering is deprecated and warns on use.

nodes.label: .specify/feature.json Handoff Record
nodes.author: github-spec-kit

nodes.label: Max 3 NEEDS CLARIFICATION Markers
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Make informed guesses and document them as Assumptions; reserve markers for choices with no reasonable default, prioritised scope > security/privacy > UX > technical detail. Caps interrogation of the user at three questions.

nodes.label: Spec Quality Checklist (checklists/requirements.md)
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Three gates — Content Quality, Requirement Completeness, Feature Readiness — re-run up to three iterations; remaining failures are documented in checklist notes and warned about rather than silently passed.

nodes.label: Technology-Agnostic Success Criteria
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Criteria must be measurable, user-focused and verifiable without implementation knowledge; 'API response under 200ms' and 'Redis cache hit rate above 80%' are rejected in favour of user-facing equivalents so the spec stays stack-neutral.

nodes.label: Task Checklist Format
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Strict '- [ ] [TaskID] [P?] [Story?] Description with file path'. Story labels are required only in user-story phases (never Setup/Foundational/Polish), and a task without an exact file path is rejected — the format is what makes tasks.md machine-parseable downstream.

nodes.label: User-Story-First Task Organization
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Grouping tasks by user story rather than by layer is what makes each story independently implementable, testable and shippable as an MVP increment; tests are opt-in and only generated when the spec or user asks for TDD.

nodes.label: The photograph-and-forward threat
nodes.rationale: A venue QR is only evidence if it cannot be photographed and forwarded. The bar to clear: no check-in without a live accomplice relaying in real time. Real-time relay is not preventable by any QR scheme and is the accepted industry bar. Non-goal: defeating a determined collusive attacker — that is a human-review problem (B8, advisory-only).

nodes.label: Option A — static per-event venue token
nodes.rationale: Smallest cost (one column, one route, one guard) but defeated by a single photograph. Evidentiary value only marginally above the current tap; recommended against for a regulator-facing record.

nodes.label: Option B — rotating QR on a staff door display
nodes.rationale: TOTP in shape: /events/{id}/door regenerates a QR every 30s from a per-event secret plus the time window; the server accepts current + one previous window for clock skew. Highest cost, but a photo is worthless in 30 seconds. Bonus: opened by an authenticated staff member, so the token can carry which staff session was at the door — a candidate fix for the credit_ledger.actor_id gap. Recommended, with C as documented fallback.

nodes.label: Option C — rotating short code, no camera
nodes.rationale: Same rotation machinery as B with no camera permission and no new scan flow. Best accessibility of the three. Practical bar is lower than B's because a short code is far easier to relay by voice or text than a QR.

nodes.label: Six failure modes of frozen hand-versioned PDFs
nodes.rationale: Stale by construction (poster frozen one day before accreditation issued, so the attendee's most important information could not be on the most-distributed artefact), no single source of truth, no personalisation, revision fan-out, dead-end artefacts that cannot update or check anyone in, and logistics trapped in a slide export.

nodes.label: Why an agency cannot copy the replacement
nodes.rationale: Their revenue depends on revision being expensive. A mechanism where revision is free cannot be offered by a business that bills per revision -- a business-model constraint, not a competence gap, and therefore the more durable kind of advantage. The displacement target is not to out-design them but to reduce their design job to supplying one hero image.

nodes.label: Design as the acquisition surface

nodes.label: Credit is (event, body, days_attended), not (event, attendance)

Multi-college is the norm at conference scale, so 'HKCP as first accrediting body' describes one row of thirteen on a real event. nodes.label: Per-activity caps live on the body, not the event
nodes.rationale: Community Medicine, O&G and Paediatricians each cap below the sum of their own per-day awards.
